applies_why: The judge text does the governed thing by using the absence of an exhibited verse statement as part of a STANDS ground.
quote: no exhibited verse says Joseph knew Mary before the birth.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: ‘a single verse does not state a link or its contrary’ — broad reading: it forbids using absence of an explicit verse statement, including ‘no exhibited verse says,’ as a ground for STANDS; narrow reading: it forbids only a one-verse omission, not absence across all exhibits.
why: D2’s STANDS ground uses the absence of an exhibited verse saying Joseph knew Mary before the birth as part of its basis, which K-S2 forbids.
